subject: Close readiness: GPU roster verification + temporary hold request (SN-2026-142)
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Close readiness: GPU roster verification + temporary hold request (SN-2026-142)

Team —

We’ve moved Supernova Labs (SN-2026-142) into final legal review; sales expect a sign by mid-June. They’ll be running a multi-tenant POC for 6–8 weeks followed by a phased production ramp starting ~2026-06-15. Before I engage procurement for a PO cadence, I need two quick things today: 

1) Inventory check: can we confirm available GPU-equivalent capacity (A100/80GB or equivalent) for the window 2026-06-15 -> 2026-09-15? I only need a conservative, reservable count and the expected impact on other committed deals.

2) Temporary hold: recommend placing a 30-day soft hold (non-binding) on the capacity while legal finishes. If we can’t hold resources, we risk losing the deal to a competitor who can guarantee capacity.

Attached: initial MRP sizing the AE collected from the customer (supernova_mrp_sizing_v1.xlsx).

Please reply with a short inventory snapshot and your recommended hold size/cadence. I’ll coordinate with Emily (procurement at Supernova) after we confirm.

Thanks,
Mateo
Mateo Alvarez
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachment: supernova_mrp_sizing_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Close readiness: GPU roster verification + temporary hold request (SN-2026-142)

Mateo —

Quick inventory snapshot based on current allocation and committed reserved capacity:
- Free equivalent (A100/80GB): 12 nodes immediately available across US-West pools
- Additional convertible capacity (quantization / 4-bit options): equivalent of ~6 A100 nodes if customer accepts Q4 quant profile
- Planned churn in mid-June (scheduled decommissions): -2 nodes (~2026-06-10)

Recommendation:
- Place a soft hold for 8 A100-equivalent nodes for 30 days (2026-06-01 -> 2026-06-30) as requested; this preserves runway for the POC without impacting existing committed customers.
- If Supernova requires full production (post-POC) guarantees, we should discuss a reserved-capacity commit (Dedicated) — I estimate they’ll need 16 nodes to hit the throughput targets in their sizing doc.

Impact notes:
- Holding 8 nodes reduces immediate buffer for smaller short-term bursts but does not violate any SLA-backed contracts.
- If they prefer lower cost vs strict latency, switching to the Q4 profile saves ~30% capacity cost and would lower the hard node count.

Attaching fleet snapshot used for this check: fleet_snapshot_20260512.csv

—Priyom
Priyom Das
Capacity Planning Lead, Redwood Inference
priyom_das@redwood.com

Attachment: fleet_snapshot_20260512.csv (CSV stub)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Close readiness: GPU roster verification + temporary hold request (SN-2026-142)

Thanks for the snapshot, Priyom — good work.

I approve the soft hold for 8 A100-equivalent units for a 30-day window. Couple of asks before we confirm to the customer: 
- Mateo: confirm contract signing target date and expected POC start date (your note said ~2026-06-15; we might want the hold to start ~2026-06-01 to account for provisioning lead time).
- Grace: please review allocation policy for this class of POC (attachment: allocation_policy_sn142.pdf) — I want clear fallback rules if traffic spikes and we need graceful degradation (fallback models, regional failover).
- Marissa: can procurement accept a soft hold without an initial PO? If not, what documentation do you need from Sales to start an express procurement workflow?

If all align, I’ll flag the scheduler to prevent double-booking in the US-West pool.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Dedicated, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Attachment: allocation_policy_sn142.pdf (policy doc stub)

From: Emily Zhao <ezhao@supernovalabs.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 15:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Close readiness: GPU roster verification + temporary hold request (SN-2026-142)

Hi Mateo —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. We’d like to request a 30-day soft hold and confirm we’re targeting a POC ramp beginning 2026-06-15 (customer internal timeline). Can you confirm the exact node count and whether the 8-node soft hold can be converted into a reserved commit if needed?

We’d prefer to keep latency at the target levels in the sizing doc; if you think switching to a quantized profile will materially affect performance, please call that out. Also include next steps and any docs we need to sign to formalize the hold.

Thanks,
Emily Zhao
Head of Procurement, Supernova Labs
ezhao@supernovalabs.com
